title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of wrapping a single LLM generator (declared gpt-5-mini) with a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair on intent→device‑configuration tasks. Following a preregistered paired shared‑initial design (cns‑m2026‑01), we evaluated 300 intents (600 episodes). Baseline generator proposals produced execution‑validated correct configurations in 299/300 tasks (99.667%); the guarded pipeline (validator ± one repair) produced 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.003333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider‑call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator + 1 repair). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSON, manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (representative paths and SHAs are cited in the Disclosure). We discuss operational interpretation, threats to validity, and reproducibility.

sections.introduction: LLM‑based intent→configuration translation promises to reduce operator burden in NetOps but introduces safety and correctness concerns (hallucinated commands, unintended policy/reachability changes). Production patterns commonly place a deterministic validator (reachability/policy checker) in front of execution and optionally invoke automated repair. Quantitative, preregistered measurements of the net effect of such generate–validate–repair (GVR) wrappers—with full per‑call archival and deterministic reproducibility—are scarce. We executed a preregistered paired experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) that (i) isolates the validator+repair marginal effect using a shared‑initial candidate design, (ii) archives every model call, provider trace, validator trace and scoring artifact, and (iii) assesses whether a single validator+≤1 repair improves the rate of execution‑validated correct configs versus the generator alone.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents LLMs for NetOps, intent translation, and verifier‑assisted pipelines; representative leads include engineering prototypes and GVR architectures that motivate verifier integration. This study differs by preregistering a paired estimand, freezing repair budgets and retry policy, and archiving full provider and validator traces for deterministic reconciliation. We follow recommended evaluation practices (predefinition of estimands, contamination checks, fixed RNG seeds for selection and bootstrap, and full artifact hashing) to improve traceability and reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study preregistration (cns‑m2026‑01; SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7) fixed primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, paired shared‑initial design, contamination/exclusion rules, repair budget (≤1 automated repair), retry policy, planned N=300, exact McNemar two‑sided confirmatory test, and bootstrap CI plan (10,000 resamples, seed=1729).

Task bank and selection: A deterministic task generator produced 300 intents by combining filtered public examples and seeded synthetic templates; deterministic contamination heuristics excluded flagged candidates. Final task manifest: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). All selection used a fixed RNG seed as preregistered.

Generator, validator, and guarded pipeline: Declared generator = gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) parsed generator candidates, simulated device state transitions in an emulator snapshot, checked task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, preserve_unspecified_state), and returned pass/fail plus structured traces. On validator failure the pipeline permitted a single automated repair call. All model calls and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/.

Shared‑initial semantics and accounting: The preregistered shared‑initial design uses the same generator candidate as the shared initial proposal for both baseline and guarded conditions to isolate the gate’s marginal effect. This choice reduces generation variance between conditions; it does not measure behavior of pipelines that independently requery the LLM per gate. Deterministic reconciliation (analysis artifact) records provider_call accounting and confirms the single repair call; see analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 = f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6).

Scoring and analysis: Per‑episode binary outcome = 1 if the validator confirms the candidate yields an execution‑validated configuration satisfying the intent with no unintended reachability/policy changes; 0 otherwise. Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided on discordant pairs (n10,n01). Confidence: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The full analysis log and seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e).
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. Planned episodes = 600 (300 intents × shared initial); completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 301 (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, per‑episode scoring JSON, and call cache entries are archived (execution/provider_calls/, execution/scoring/, execution/call_cache/). Representative artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 cited above), and analysis artifacts (see Disclosure).

Aggregates and primary inference. Baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0) (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 55eacb88c64f29dc...). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d...): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The analysis implementation, seeds, and bootstrap parameters are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 cited above) to enable exact reproduction of p and CI.

Why p = 1.0 with discordant (1,0). In small‑sample exact McNemar enumeration the two‑sided p aggregates probabilities of tables at least as or more extreme than the observed under the null of marginal equality; with n10=1 and n01=0, this computation (as implemented in our archived analysis executor) yields p=1.0. The exact implementation and seed are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256 cited) so readers may recompute one‑sided or alternative exact formulations if preferred.

Repair and failure diagnostics. Repair calls: 299 tasks required zero repairs; 1 task required a single automated repair (repair trace archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). No guarded residual failures remained. Per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/) include validator violation codes and diagnostic fields (validator_violation_codes, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count) and are archived for forensic inspection. Representative per‑episode artifacts for pair‑000001..000006 are included in the archive and referenced in the Disclosure.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. In this controlled emulator corpus the generator already achieved near‑ceiling success; the guarded GVR pipeline corrected the single baseline failure using one repair call at minimal extra model‑call cost. In regimes where generator error rates are higher or tasks are more adversarial, the same validator+repair pattern would likely yield larger absolute operational gains. The shared‑initial design isolates the gate’s marginal effect (same candidate), but does not evaluate pipelines that requery the LLM per condition; the choice was preregistered to improve internal isolation. The deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 cited above) documents provider_call accounting and confirms the single repair invocation.

Construct and external validity. The validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; production safety exposures (live, multi‑domain interactions, hardware variants, human operators) are broader. Only one declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; we do not claim multi‑model generality. The task bank is a mixture of filtered public items and seeded deterministic synthetic templates; results therefore speak to controlled intent distributions similar to those artifacts.

Practical implications. For operators with low baseline generator error rates, a deterministic validator plus a small repair budget can eliminate isolated generator mistakes with small overhead. System designers should consider validator coverage, repair budget, latency/cost tradeoffs, and whether to requery the generator when the validator rejects a proposal. The archived artifacts allow teams to evaluate these tradeoffs with the exact run data.
sections.conclusion: We report a fully preregistered paired evaluation (cns‑m2026‑01) of a generator (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic validator+≤1 repair wrapper on 300 intent→configuration tasks. Baseline success = 299/300; guarded success = 300/300. Paired difference = 0.003333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider calls used = 301 (300 generator + 1 repair). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSON, manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed; representative paths and SHAs are cited in the Disclosure Statement. The guarded GVR pattern corrected the isolated error at very low extra cost; extension to higher‑error distributions, multi‑model comparisons, and iterative repair budgets remains for future work, using the same preregistration and archival practices to preserve traceability.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (archived references and runtime facts)

Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: cns-m2026-01 (frozen study plan) — preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7. The preregistration defined the research question, primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), paired shared‑initial design, repair budget (≤1), inclusion/exclusion and contamination checks, analysis plan (exact McNemar two‑sided; bootstrap CI 10,000 resamples, seed=1729), and retry/missingness rules.

Declared LLM(s) and model identifiers: gpt-5-mini as the declared generator; configuration archived at execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820. Provider family: recorded under execution/provider_calls/ (full per‑call traces archived).

Orchestration, validator, and repair framework: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) — implemented to parse generator candidates, simulate device state transitions in a closed emulator snapshot, and deterministically check reachability/policy invariants and task‑specific constraints. Repair policy: single automated repair attempt permitted when the validator rejects a candidate (preregistered budget ≤1). Representative repair trace archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba.

Artifacts and reproducibility archive (representative):
- Raw run outputs and results: execution/raw_results.jsonl — SHA‑256: 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb.
- Task manifest (final selected N=300): execution/task_manifest.jsonl — SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990.
- Model configuration: execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820.
- Analysis artifacts and exact analysis log (seeds, bootstrap params, implementation used to compute McNemar & CI): analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256: 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e.
- Paired contingency CSV used for the primary test: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv — SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55.
- Deterministic reconciliation and provider_call audit: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json — SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6.
- Representative per‑episode artifacts (examples): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt — SHA‑256: 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json — SHA‑256: 2e4a1ef1389a18cfc5a0d6728d0978879c6675125b090b66c2dbd97b730ef153.

Autonomy statement and human roles: Before the autonomy lock the Research Director (human) selected the topic family (Generative AI/LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial master prompt archive above. After the autonomy lock the AI system autonomously executed literature review, gap selection, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, experiment execution, all model calls (archived), validator runs, scoring, analysis, drafting, AI‑based peer review, and revision. No manual human edits were made to substantive manuscript content after the autonomy lock; all substantive text derives from the autonomous run and archived artifacts.

Deviations and technical restarts: The run completed without failed episodes (completed episodes = 600; failed = 0). Provider call accounting shows 301 model calls (300 shared‑initial generator calls + 1 repair call) as recorded in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 cited). Any automated retries followed the preregistered retry policy (≤2 retries for transient failures) and are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl; the execution manifest contains full per‑call hashes.

Limitations (brief): single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) so no multi‑model generality; closed‑emulator validator reflects deterministic reachability checks in a snapshot and may omit production dynamics; shared‑initial semantics isolates marginal gate effect but does not measure pipelines that requery the LLM per condition; repair budget limited to one automated attempt. See manuscript Limitations section for full discussion.

I certify that the above factual disclosure statements, artifact paths, and SHA‑256 values are copied from the archived run artifacts associated with this submission and are not invented.
limitations: Ceiling baseline: baseline success = 299/300 reduces power to detect larger preregistered improvements.

Task scope and external validity: deterministic emulator‑backed intent corpus (mixed public + synthetic); results do not directly generalize to noisy, adversarial, or human‑authored intent distributions in production.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini); no multi‑model generality claimed.
Validator construct validity: safety operationalized as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability changes in a closed snapshot; production safety surfaces may be broader.
Repair budget constraint: only a single automated repair attempt was permitted; iterative multi‑call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
